correctness.rationale: The two ordered-particle equations imply exactly three gap drift modes f_s=-lambda*y+2g/y+2v*s with mode-specific jump rates 2gamma and gamma. The extrema are positive a=(sqrt(v²+2lambda*g)-v)/lambda, b=(sqrt(v²+2lambda*g)+v)/lambda. Synchronous contraction and accessibility select one stationary law in a fixed ordering sector. On each edge, zero current forces the outgoing small-flux magnitude q to equal the sum of competing inward fluxes. Thus 0<=u/q<=1 and a scalar logarithmic derivative q′/q has singular term 2gamma/(kappa*z) plus O(1) remainder. Integration gives strictly positive finite asymptotic coefficient; other modes are lower order. This independently yields theta_a=gamma/lambda(1-v/h), theta_b=gamma/lambda(1+v/h), all phase boundaries and identities. Pure Python checker provided as CHECK.py passed 96 assertions, including an independently discretized finite-volume stationary generator; finite checks are corroboration only. No unsupported global smoothness or full interior solution is claimed.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparison locates general interacting-pair equations and zero-flux stationary ODE in arXiv:2105.11838v1; they are acknowledged as prior. This source even plots a repulsive f(y)=1/y-lambda*y configuration and establishes the spin-dependent support. It does not explicitly calculate the two non-equal separation-edge exponents, their two critical tumbling rates or the parameter-independent exponent sum. arXiv:2302.02937v1 studies the same active-Dyson model and finite-N single-particle position marginals, not the derived stationary spacing-edge theorem. arXiv:1910.10083v1 classifies edge behavior for a linear restoring drift (equal endpoint linearization), not the unequal nonlinear gap slopes. Relevant published-finding corpus semantic searches returned scientifically noncovering works; this is not proof of uniqueness. A close source general equations may imply the present explicit asymptotic calculation under further boundary analysis; priority risk is explicitly retained. A separately inspected 2019 gap-statistics paper concerns hard-core exclusion on a ring, not inverse-distance repulsion in a harmonic trap.

value.rationale: The interparticle separation in a repulsively coupled active Dyson pair is a physically meaningful clustering observable different from the previously analyzed one-point particle position density. Its two extreme gaps have mathematically different relaxation slopes, yielding an open interval of flip rates where the small-gap density is singular while the large-gap density vanishes, followed by a second boundary transition. The two exact thresholds and universal sum rule classify the entire positive-parameter family and expose coupling-independent structure. This is a natural model-specific invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter slice, tabulation or numerical coefficient.
